findings.title: Wrong metric function called on Storage.Create error
findings.body: When `d.Storage.Create` fails, the code calls `d.recordLegacyDuration(true, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startStorage)` instead of `d.recordStorageDuration(...)`. This records a unified storage failure under the legacy metric, producing misleading observability data and making it impossible to correctly monitor storage vs legacy error rates.

findings.title: Wrong metric function called on Storage.Update error
findings.body: When `d.Storage.Update` fails, the code calls `d.recordLegacyDuration(true, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startStorage)` instead of `d.recordStorageDuration(...)`. This is the same class of bug as the Create method: a unified storage failure is recorded under the legacy duration metric, corrupting monitoring data.

findings.title: Wrong metric function called for legacy DeleteCollection result
findings.body: Inside the goroutine that asynchronously writes to legacy storage for DeleteCollection, the code calls `d.recordStorageDuration(err != nil, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startLegacy)` instead of `d.recordLegacyDuration(...)`. This records the legacy operation's outcome under the storage metric, inverting the observability semantics.

findings.title: Inconsistent metric label: `name` used instead of `options.Kind`
findings.body: In the Delete method's success path, `d.recordStorageDuration(false, mode3Str, name, method, startStorage)` passes the object `name` (e.g. "foo") as the kind label instead of `options.Kind`. Every other call in the file uses `options.Kind` for this parameter. This will produce metrics with incorrect kind labels, making dashboards and alerts based on kind unreliable.

findings.title: Delete method sets context logger to `d.Log` instead of enriched `log`
findings.body: Line 96 creates `log := d.Log.WithValues("name", name, "kind", options.Kind, "method", method)` but line 97 sets `ctx = klog.NewContext(ctx, d.Log)` using the base logger without the added values. The enriched `log` variable is only used for the error message on line 102, but any downstream code that extracts the logger from context will miss the name/kind/method fields. This should be `ctx = klog.NewContext(ctx, log)`.

findings.title: Async legacy writes derive from request context and may be silently cancelled
findings.body: All async goroutines (Create, Delete, Update, DeleteCollection) create a timeout context derived from the incoming request context (`ctx`). If the HTTP request completes and its context is cancelled before the goroutine executes, the derived context is immediately done and the legacy write silently fails. Since mode 3's stated purpose is to write to legacy 'as a safe measure', these writes should use `context.WithoutCancel(ctx)` or `context.Background()` to ensure they are not tied to the request lifecycle.

findings.title: Tests do not verify that async legacy writes actually execute
findings.body: The mode 3 tests set up mock expectations for legacy Create/Update/Delete/DeleteCollection but never wait for or assert that the goroutines actually ran. Since the legacy writes are fire-and-forget goroutines, the tests can pass even if the goroutines never execute (e.g., due to context cancellation or scheduling). The tests should use synchronization (e.g., a WaitGroup, channel, or eventually-style assertion) to confirm the legacy mock was called.
